newsitem.title: UK: UK opt-out of EMU won't harm London's position - BOE.
newsitem.headline: UK opt-out of EMU won't harm London's position - BOE.

text.p: London's pre-eminence as an international financial centre will not be eroded if Britain opts out of monetary union, the Bank of England said.
BOE executive director Ian Plenderleith, addressing a conference in London, cited an array of arguments why London's position would not be damaged.

London is international and so far more than just a European centre, Plenderleith said. It had not suffered from financial market modernisation in the main continental European centres nor from the long-standing uncertainty over British participation in the single currency, he declared.

The economics of international financial activity favoured concentration in one centre with London the preferred choice. London also had distinctive strengths and had made major advances in improving its infrastructure.
"I can think of a lot of reasons for being confident of London maintaining its international position even if we do not join the monetary union," said Plenderleith.
